title: Hosted API client adaptor UX and error surrogates playbook
summary: Working playbook that sketches a minimal client adaptor surface, error-surrogate primitives for flaky networks, and pragmatic SDK ergonomics for streaming tool-calls and structured frames.
body:
Context:
This is a working playbook — targeted at product, SDK, and runtime teams — outlining a small, deliberate set of client-side primitives and contract guarantees that make hosted streaming + tool-calling dependable for mobile and low-bandwidth clients. We want something lighter than full session persistence but robust enough for common flaky-network failure modes, and that composes well with existing tool-call semantics (idempotency, side effects, structured JSON frames).

Motivation / problem statement:
- Customers embed hosted streaming endpoints in mobile/web apps. Network disruptions (carrier handoffs, sleep, transient proxies) cause truncated streams and dropped tool-calls, producing inconsistent UIs and lost user actions.
- Full resumable session protocols are heavy for many clients (cost, implementation complexity).
- SDK ergonomics today push complexity to app teams (manual reconnection logic, heavyweight checkpoints).
- We need pragmatic defaults that keep majority of flows resilient with minimal SDK surface.

High-level goals:
1) Make streamed partial outputs (progressive text, structured action frames) easy to resume or gracefully degrade.
2) Ensure tool-calls triggered from streamed output are either safely hedged or backed by idempotent transaction primitives.
3) Provide SDK ergonomics that are tiny (3–6 APIs), easy to instrument, and straightforward to integrate in React Native and Node.
4) Minimize server-side state and retention costs. Server-side weak state (short lived caches, token-kept checkpoints) is acceptable.

Non-goals:
- Full multi-client session synchronization and CRDT-style merge.
- Guaranteeing strong transactional ACID semantics for arbitrary external tool endpoints.

Core concepts and primitives (client-facing):
1) Stream frames + Frame-IDs
   - All streaming payloads are delivered as framed events. Each frame has a monotonic frame_id (UUID4) and an offset.
   - Frame types: "text_fragment", "action_frame", "meta_checkpoint", "error_hint".
   - Clients ack checkpoints; runtime keeps short lived checkpoint windows for resumption.

2) Soft checkpoints (meta_checkpoint)
   - Periodic lightweight checkpoints carrying: last_frame_id, model_version, applied-tool-call-ids (list of opaque ids), sequence cursors.
   - Checkpoints are not a full session log — just enough to resume generation without re-running expensive front-loaded context.

3) Error surrogates
   - When a network interruption is detected, client SDK emits an "error_surrogate" locally: a small synthesized UI artifact that explains partial state (e.g., "partial summary available, last action attempted: search(order-123)").
   - Error surrogates are deterministic clients-side reconstructions based on last acknowledged checkpoint + last local events. They are intentionally conservative (no speculative tool-calls).

4) Hedged tool-call semantics
   - Tool-calls invoked by the model are wrapped in a tool-call envelope with fields: tool_call_id (opaque), idempotency_token, expected_side_effect_hint.
   - SDK by default issues the tool-call optimistically to the host runtime via a hedged policy: primary call to customer's tool endpoint + fallback control-plane queuing for reliable delivery (if primary fails).
   - Runtime exposes a stable "tool-call status" endpoint clients can poll post-resume to check if a call completed.

5) Resume API patterns (3 methods)
   - resume_from_checkpoint(checkpoint_token, on_frame_cb) -> reconnects and streams frames starting after checkpoint.
   - replay_last_n(n, mode="best_effort") -> ask the server to re-emit recent frames for UI reconstruction when checkpoints are unavailable.
   - attach_offline_cache(cache_id) -> local caching of small action frames to rehydrate UI fast on reconnection.

Example SDK ergonomics (JS pseudocode):
- Minimal surface (3–5 methods): openStream(opts), resumeStream(opts), onFrame(cb), closeStream(reason)

const s = client.openStream({model: 'gpt-6b-lite', sessionHints: {user_id}})
s.onFrame(frame => {
  if (frame.type === 'text_fragment') renderAppend(frame.text)
  if (frame.type === 'action_frame') {
    // action_frame contains tool_call_id and a contract
    showActionCandidate(frame.action)
    client.confirmAction(frame.tool_call_id)
  }
})
// On reconnect
client.resumeStream({checkpoint_token: lastCheckpoint}, s.onFrame)

Edge cases and UX examples:
- Mobile backgrounding: connection drops during a long stream that triggered two tool-calls. Client receives a meta_checkpoint before backgrounding. On foreground, resumeStream is called automatically; server replays frames after checkpoint and emits tool-call-status for each tool_call_id. App shows "Action succeeded" or "Action needs retry".
- No checkpoint available: client uses replay_last_n(50) to reconstruct last 50 frames. This may re-run side-effect-free parts but must not re-trigger non-idempotent tool calls.

Server-side runtime notes (implementation hints):
- Keep short-lived checkpoint store keyed by session_token with TTL 2–5 minutes (configurable per-customer).
- Tool-call envelope is recorded with tool_call_id and idempotency_token; runtime ensures deduplication for identical tokens within a retention window.
- Provide a lightweight tool-call-status API and a replay window API.

Observability & telemetry:
- Emit telemetry events: checkpoint_created, checkpoint_ack, resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_fallback_replay, toolcall_initiated, toolcall_status_change.
- Surface per-route SLOs for resume latency and replay accuracy.

Acceptance criteria (for a small pilot):
- SDK exposes the three resume primitives and stream framing with frame_id in both RN and Node SDKs.
- Runtime stores checkpoints and can resume provider-hosted streams for 80% of mobile foreground reconnect scenarios within 3s.
- Tool-call deduplication works for idempotency_tokens across 24h window in pilot infra.
- Telemetry shows meaningful reduction in "orphaned-action" incidents for pilot customers (target: 50% drop).

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Backwards compatibility: clients using older SDKs receive frames but without resume tokens; runtime will fall back to best-effort replay.
- Migration path: enable framed streams for new routes first (beta flag) and collect instrumentation before broad rollout.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Checkpoint frequency vs bandwidth: more frequent checkpoints help resume but increase meta payloads. Need empirical tuning per model/route.
- How to represent uncertain tool-call side-effect hints in the model output? Model writers need guidance to avoid ambiguity.
- Long-term: evaluate a compact CRDT-ish session layer if customers show need for multi-device session sync.

Next steps (short timeline):
- 1 week: core SDK API sketch and minimal API contract proto (Elena).
- 2 weeks: runtime checkpoint prototype + tool-call-status prototype (Marco).
- 3 weeks: RN + Node pilot SDK + telemetry hooks (Jordan + Asha).
- 6 weeks: small customer pilot (1 mid-size customer), iterate.

Notes to reviewers:
- Looking for feedback on the hedging default (do we expose hedging knobs per customer?), and on the API names (resumeStream vs resume_from_checkpoint). Also please review the user-visible wording for error_surrogate artifacts — want to avoid implying false guarantees.

Scratchpad / ideas to preserve:
- Consider exposing a "surrogate_template" in the checkpoint so clients can render consistent error surrogates across platforms.
- Small UX nicety: allow clients to request a "concise-summary-on-resume" flag so server emits a short summary frame to help reorientation.
- Potential follow-up: structured verification frames for tool outputs (signed/hashed) for high-assurance enterprise flows.

References:
- See linked artifacts for existing handshake notes and GH PR.
- Internal notes: evaluate UTC-relative checkpoint TTL vs per-customer configured TTL.
